blocks.raw: # Securities lending

**Fully Paid Securities Lending** (FPSL) is a practice in which DriveWealth can lend customers’ securities to other financial institutions. This generates interest revenue which is typically shared with the customer and the client firm.
blocks.text: Fully Paid Securities Lending (FPSL) is a practice in which DriveWealth can lend customers’ securities to other financial institutions. This generates interest revenue which is typically shared with the customer and the client firm.

blocks.raw:
<Callout icon="🚧" theme="warn">
  ### Associated risks

  Securities lending activities increase risks for customers including loss of SIPC protection. Consider these risks before enabling access to this feature.
</Callout>

blocks.raw: ## Receiving loan interest

DriveWealth automatically monitors opted-in Accounts and their Positions. When possible, the assets will be loaned to other financial institutions, based on demand and interest rates. The customer can always sell their assets, even if they are on loan.
blocks.text: DriveWealth automatically monitors opted-in Accounts and their Positions. When possible, the assets will be loaned to other financial institutions, based on demand and interest rates. The customer can always sell their assets, even if they are on loan.

blocks.raw: A unique type of Transaction will be posted to an Account each month for the interest it received. There may be months where no interest is generated, and no Transaction will be created.
blocks.text: A unique type of Transaction will be posted to an Account each month for the interest it received. There may be months where no interest is generated, and no Transaction will be created.

blocks.raw: ## Other effects during a loan

Although a customer won’t see in real-time what positions are on loan, they will receive an additional page in their [Month-end Statements](https://developer.drivewealth.com/apis/docs/official-documents) Month-end Statement with details like:
blocks.text: Although a customer won’t see in real-time what positions are on loan, they will receive an additional page in their Month-end Statements Month-end Statement with details like:

blocks.raw:
* The date in which the positions were out on loan
* How much of their positions were on loan
* The accrued rebate for that date
* The collateral associated with that position
blocks.text: The date in which the positions were out on loanHow much of their positions were on loanThe accrued rebate for that dateThe collateral associated with that position

blocks.raw: Additionally, while positions are loaned, customers do not receive dividends directly from the issuer. Instead, the borrowing party receives those dividends, then repays them. In effect, this means a customer with positions on loan receives a **Manufactured Dividend**, which looks very similar to a regular dividend when posted as a Transaction:
